0.text: Because it's the one check that keeps slipping: protein was short on 6 of the last 7 days, and today you're at 96 of 165 g. Everything else is in good shape, calories, steps and logging all met, so protein is what's holding your on-track days at 1 of 7. During your veg period the easiest fix is a whey scoop and a katori of soya or paneer at dinner, which adds about 45 g.

It's possible but tight on a strict veg diet: you'd need protein at every meal, something like a whey shake, paneer or tofu at lunch and dinner, soya chunks and curd. Today you're at 96 g with your usual meals, so the gap is about 70 g. Two whey scoops plus 150 g paneer would close most of it.
Good day: 1880 of 2200 kcal, 9400 steps and your evening walk done. Protein is 96 of 110 g, a touch under, so a glass of milk or a bowl of curd before bed would round it off.

10 kg in a month isn't safe; it would be mostly water and muscle and would bounce back. I suggest at most about 0.8 kg a week for you, so roughly 3 to 3.5 kg by the wedding, which will already show in photos. Want me to set a goal for the wedding date at that pace, with 74 kg still the longer target?

Yes, especially if you're fairly new to lifting: eating near your 120 g protein and getting stronger on your three gym days lets you build muscle while the calorie gap takes off fat. The scale moves slower that way, so your body fat readings (24% down to 22.8%) are the better sign it's working.

That's water, not fat: a salty, carb-heavy wedding meal holds 1 to 2 kg of water for a couple of days, and 1.5 kg of fat would take over 11,000 extra kcal. Go back to your normal meals and steps, and it'll settle in two or three days. Your weekly weigh-in is what counts.

At your current pace of 0.55 kg a week you'd reach 74 kg around 8 February 2027, about a week after your 31 January deadline. You need 0.62 kg a week to hit it on time, so a slightly tighter week or two now would close that.
